content: Distribution and traction transformers are sampled annually for dissolved gas analysis. A confirmation sample is taken within 30 days when hydrogen exceeds 150 ppm or acetylene is detected. Oil is not topped up before sampling because dilution masks fault gases. Results are recorded against the asset number in the maintenance system.

Stationary lead-acid batteries supporting switchgear control are capacity-tested every 12 months. A string is replaced when it retains less than 80 percent of rated capacity. Electrolyte level and terminal torque are checked quarterly. Battery rooms are ventilated and hydrogen alarms are tested at the same interval.

Track geometry is measured by recording cars at least every three months on passenger lines. Gauge, cant, twist and alignment are compared with the line standard. Immediate action is required for gauge widening beyond 25 mm on plain line; a temporary speed restriction is applied until the tamping possession.

Ultrasonic rail flaw detection covers every running line twice a year, and curved rail with a radius below 400 m four times a year. Suspect defects are hand-tested the same day. A confirmed transverse defect over 20 percent of head area requires a speed restriction and a planned rail replacement.

Overhead line equipment is visually inspected every six months, with a full tension and stagger measurement annually. Contact wire height is checked against the electrification standard. Arcing horns, insulators and section insulators are photographed. Defects that could cause dewirement are reported as immediate.

Signalling assets are designed to fail safe: a track circuit failure places signals at danger and does not permit a route to set. The signaller reports the failure, the duty technician attends, and train movements continue only under pilot working. The incident log records the asset, the failure mode and the time to restore.

Level crossings are inspected monthly for road markings, sighting distances, barrier operation and warning lights. The annual test includes the obstacle detection system and the power changeover. Any crossing with a history of misuse is reviewed for upgrade to full barriers or closure.

Vegetation within three metres of the running line is cut before the growing season and re-inspected in late summer. Trees that could strike the overhead line are removed within falling distance. Herbicide is not applied within ten metres of a watercourse; a catchment consent is required.

Transformer tap changers are exercised through their full range during the annual service. Contact resistance is measured and compared with the commissioning record. A tap changer that shows inconsistent stepping or a rise in contact resistance is taken out of service for inspection rather than left on manual.

Distribution mains are monitored by district metered areas with nightly minimum-flow analysis. A step change in minimum night flow above 5 percent triggers a leak survey. Acoustic loggers and correlators locate the burst before excavation. Pressure is reduced overnight where transient pressures exceed the pipe rating.

Combined sewer overflows are monitored by level and rainfall telemetry. A spill event is recorded when the overflow operates for more than 15 minutes. Screens and telemetry are inspected monthly, and the regulator is notified within 24 hours of an unpermitted discharge.

Gas district governors are serviced annually and pressure-tested every five years. Outlet pressure is checked against the licence set point, and the slam-shut is tripped to prove closure. A governor that drifts more than 5 percent from set point is overhauled rather than adjusted.

Smart electricity meters are commissioned with the tariff, time zone and communication profile verified before handover. A meter that fails to register consumption within 24 hours is treated as a commissioning failure. Gas meters additionally require a tightness test and a check of the regulator.

High-voltage switching is performed under a permit-to-work with a documented isolation, proved dead and earthed at the point of work. The authorised person and the control engineer confirm the switching schedule. Live working is permitted only under a separate live-work authorisation.

SCADA alarm rationalisation keeps the standing alarm count below 20 per shift. Repeating alarms are inhibited only with a time limit and a work order. Analogue points are dead-banded to avoid alarm chatter; all inhibits are reviewed monthly.

Asset criticality combines safety consequence, supply interruption and repair cost on a 1-to-5 scale. Criticality drives inspection frequency and spares holding. A criticality review is triggered by a change in network topology or a repeat failure of the same asset class.

Underground cable faults are located by time-domain reflectometry, then confirmed by a surge generator and acoustic pinpointing. The cable is spiked and earthed before jointers expose it. A repaired joint is pressure-tested and the route record updated with the joint location.

Water treatment works record turbidity and chlorine residual continuously. A turbidity reading above 1 NTU for more than 15 minutes triggers a shutdown of the affected filter and a resample. Chlorine residual below 0.2 mg per litre at the works outlet is treated as a loss of disinfection.

Gas pressure loggers on medium-pressure mains record hourly. A sustained rise above the maximum operating pressure is reported to the control room immediately. The area is walked to look for a failed regulator or a closed valve before any pressure reduction is applied.
